role: independent_explorer: query-menu ranking (joint vs per-circuit information)
hypothesis: Remaining unreliability sits in the pinning phase, not in the rule reading or the final pick: the parent ranks queries by how evenly they split ONE circuit's distinct tables, ignoring the inventory coupling and the fact that the answer is a joint 24-bit table, and offers 8 options of which the model often takes a weak one. Ranking queries by how evenly they split the joint (A,B,C) tables still allowed, and showing only the best 3, raises the expected information per query and removes coupling-dead queries. On the 18-query budget this cuts the number of instances whose circuits are still unpinned when the budget runs out, which matters most on NOT-heavy inventories. Falsifiable: if per-query expected joint information does not rise vs the parent on the same instances, or if simulated over-budget rates do not drop, the hypothesis is wrong.
behavior_changes: Space.joint(): enumerates distinct joint tables (A | B<<8 | C<<16) consistent with rules + answers, summed over inventory allocations; returns None if the rules are contradicted or the enumeration exceeds 300k.
Harness._joint_splits(): scores each (circuit, input) query by the binary entropy of its split of the joint set.

Before pinning, the model sees 'N combinations of tables A, B, C are still possible' and only the top-3 joint-ranked queries with their counts, instead of 8 per-circuit-ranked ones. The per-circuit candidate listing is unchanged.

A pick outside the top 3 is re-asked, and the feedback says it splits the combinations less evenly. Any splitting query is accepted on the last try. The fallback after all tries now prefers a splitting pick over a useless one.
When the joint set is unavailable (too large, or the rules were contradicted and the space relaxed), the parent's per-circuit ranking and 8-item menu are used unchanged.
preserved_behaviors: The model writes every query, and the harness never sends a query the model did not write.
Rule-derived candidate space (two 2-input gates per circuit plus NOTs, exact inventory split) and its per-circuit degradation on contradiction.
Verification phase: once every circuit is pinned, the leftover budget is spent on model-chosen checks, testing the coupling-only rows first and then unseen rows.
Final guess assembled from the model's numbered per-circuit picks among consistent candidates.
verification: Ran check_b1r1_cand_pilot_strict_b10g3r2_b1r1g1.py: 10/10 status=ok, parsed_final_guess=True, 18 queries each, 19-21 solver calls (model mostly accepted on the first ask).

Replayed every answer through the rule space: all 10 end with exactly one consistent (A,B,C), no relaxation, 0 contradictions across all verification checks. The final 24-bit guesses are identical to the parent's on all 10 instances (compared guess strings, not outcomes).

Expected joint information per pinning-phase query (label-free, computed from the history): child 0.890 bits vs parent 0.815, g0 0.836, g2 0.821. Joint-zero-information queries: child 0, parent 3, g2 2.

Queries needed to pin all circuits: child mean 10.9 (max 14) vs parent 11.4 (max 15). This depends on how the answers fall: child is worse on i130 (9 vs 6) and i228 (13 vs 10), and on i228 the joint set went 3924 -> 1 in 13 queries, close to the log2 floor of 12.

Offline simulation over 150 sampled rule-consistent truths per inventory, comparing greedy policies (per-circuit vs joint ranking) and random picks among the top 8 per-circuit vs the top 3 joint. Over-budget (>18 queries to pin): {3 AND,3 OR,3 NOT}: per-circuit top-8 random 33/150 vs joint top-3 random 5/150. {2 AND,4 OR,2 NOT}: 2/150 vs 0/150. Inventories with 0-2 NOTs: 0 in both.
Menu position the model picked: 1st 50, 2nd 15, 3rd 44, outside 0. Mean loss vs the best option is 0.017 bits (max 0.35), so a 3-option menu costs little and keeps a real choice with the model.
risks: On this batch every harness already pins all circuits within budget, so the gain shows only in information per query and in simulation, not in a different final table here.

Inventories whose joint enumeration exceeds 300k (e.g. 3 AND/3 OR with 4+ NOTs, about 250k-540k before dedupe) fall back to the parent's per-circuit ranking. Near the cap, each turn costs roughly a second of Python.
A 3-item menu narrows the model's choice. If the model fixates on menu position 3 when options are far from tied, information drops, though the observed loss is small.
Fewer queries to pin means more go to the verification phase. That helps only if the rule reading could be wrong, and so far 0 contradictions have been seen across all branches.
